public_rationale: Bloomberg reported financing strain on October 28, 2026, while also reporting tens of billions in new financing that week [e1]. Crunchbase reported substantial AI fundraising in October, including DeepSeek's $15.9 billion round [e2]. These reports do not establish that both financing conditions occurred across a substantial part of the market, or that the boom ended [e1, e2]. Continued fundraising before both conditions are established does not contradict the conditional forecast [e1, e2].
limitations: Higher yields and difficulty distributing debt do not establish broad financing unavailability [e1].
Large successful rounds do not establish dependable funding for the wider startup population [e2].
Neither item establishes an end to the boom or durable continuation after both financing conditions occur [e1, e2].

statement.excerpt: As I’ve said for a while, all of this ends when the money runs out — when seemingly-unlimited data center debt becomes distressingly hard to raise, and when AI startups can’t rely on the perpetual availability of venture capital to keep them alive.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is a broad end to the AI investment boom after both financing conditions occur, rather than an isolated funding failure or stock-market decline.
Both conditions must be established across a substantial part of the relevant market.
The speaker supplies neither a deadline nor a lag between financing exhaustion and the boom ending. No numerical threshold or observation window is imposed.
criteria.support_condition: Both financing conditions occur, followed by a clearly established end to the AI investment boom associated with that financing withdrawal.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Both financing conditions occur, but decisive evidence establishes that the investment boom continues through a durable replacement funding model. A short interval without collapse is insufficient.
